champion: Squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue
ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bulbar and neck symptoms with weight loss
salient_findings: Constant pain at right occipital and cervical paraspinal areas
key_facts: Three-year history of worsening dysarthria and dysphagia
Choking episodes provoked when lying supine
One-year history of constant pain at right occipital and cervical paraspinal areas
20-pound weight loss
Right tongue deviation and atrophy
Limited tongue movements and difficulty with tongue protrusion
Lingual and palatal dysarthria
Normal laboratory tests including Acetylcholine receptor antibodies, TSH, B12, ANA, ESR, and CK
Active denervation changes on EMG
Infiltrative process at the base and root of the tongue on MRI
Enhancing, infiltrative, and partially necrotic mass on Maxillofacial CT
Focal, non-keratinizing invasive squamous cell carcinoma on biopsy
